messages:
alex (eng-platform): Heads up — we need a concrete plan for canary/weighted routing in the gateway. Product wants 10->30->60 rollouts for model variants, plus header-based override for partners. How do we represent this in the route config and ensure telemetry + quotas still make sense?

maya (eng-runtime): I can sketch a YAML config for weighted routes. main questions: sticky sessions (user-level consistency) and where sampler lives. quick sketch: 
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: header x-customer-tier == premium
weights:
  model-v1: 0.9
  model-v2-canary: 0.1
sticky_key: user_id
overrides:
  header: x-force-model
```
This keeps config at gateway.

liam (product): We need the header override for enterprise customers (for testing). Also request: canary rules should support percent-by-user or percent-by-request. Prefers user-based so session quality is consistent.

alex (eng-platform): Agreed on user-based. But if the gateway does the weight split, do we get per-model telemetry (latency, errors) tied to the request for the control plane to decide automatic rollbacks? We need precise counts for billing too.

sasha (eng-sre): Important: quotas. If partner overrides a header, we must still attribute tokens to the customer and enforce rate limits. That suggests decision must happen before the quota check or quotas need to be model-aware. Also: we need to avoid split-induced spikes on backend capacity.

zoe (devex): UX ask: console should show a simulated traffic distribution and an expected qps per model (given recent traffic). Also provide one-click rollout ramp and auto-rollback thresholds. Can we expose a dry-run that annotates a sample of last-hour requests to show where they'd go?

maya (eng-runtime): Two architecture choices: (A) gateway-level deterministic hashing + weight logic (fast, single hop). Pros: low latency, simple. Cons: telemetry attribution requires tagging and propagating model variant chosen to backend and logging. (B) control-plane router (preflight service) that returns a model id, then gateway forwards — pros: central metrics + audit, easier sync with rollouts; cons: extra RPC on request path and scaling complexity.

nora (eng-platform): For (B) we can cache routing decisions per user for X minutes to reduce RPCs. But cache invalidation during ramp changes is a pain — need to invalidate affected keys on rollout. That's doable via pubsub but adds complexity.

liam (product): From product POV, prefer (B) because it lets us query the rollout state and simulate. But we can't have 1 extra network call for every token request; that kills latency. Could we hybridize? Control plane decides and pushes a consistent config (hash ranges) to gateways for local decision.

alex (eng-platform): Hybrid sounds promising: control plane computes ranges (e.g., hash(user_id) in [0,1000) maps to model-v2) and pushes to gateways. Gateways do deterministic routing locally. Advantages: local fast decisions + centralized audit + rollouts as config deltas. We need a schema for ranges and a versioned rollout resource.

maya (eng-runtime): Implementation note: need to guarantee deterministic hash function across versions and languages. Also when weights change, we need to smoothly migrate by updating config version and optionally include a migration window for sticky keys.

sasha (eng-sre): Monitoring hooks: per-variant metrics (5xx rate, p95 latency, token consumption) and anomaly detectors. Add a safety gate: if p95 latency > baseline * 1.5 or error rate > 0.5% absolute, auto-roll back the canary. Also we should rate-limit canary spillover to protect capacity.

zoe (devex): Console UX: rollout modal with sliders for percent, a toggle for 'user-based' vs 'request-based', checkboxes for header overrides, and a preview button that runs the dry-run on sampled logs. Also show estimated cost delta.

alex (eng-platform): Quotas: propose model-aware quota checks. Gateway consults local route decision and then performs quota check with (customer, model_id) tuple. That keeps enforcement local. We must ensure billing mapping uses that model_id.

maya (eng-runtime): Telemetry path: gateway injects headers: x-chosen-model, x-rollout-version, x-rollout-key into request to backend. Backends will emit those into tracing and metrics. We'll need to update ingestion to attribute by model.

nora (eng-platform): Edge case: partner header override should honor allowlist. We should support a per-customer override policy. Config example: 
```json
{"allow_overrides": ["cust-123","cust-789"], "force_header": "x-force-model"}
```

liam (product): Nice. Also add a canary schedule API: start_time, target_percent, duration, ramps. And an audit log.

sasha (eng-sre): Rollout automation: do not allow >20% increase in tokens to new model in a single step. Otherwise runbook: auto pause + alert to #oncall if violated.

alex (eng-platform): OK action items: (1) maya + nora to draft rollout resource schema (hash ranges, versioning, allowlist, analytics hooks) (2) maya to prototype gateway local decision using pushed ranges (3) zoe to design console dry-run UX + preview API (4) sasha to write SLO-based safety gate rules for auto-rollback (5) liam to define product rollout API.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for rollout v2024-07-12-137 (applied to gateways 3/3) :rocket:

liam (product): thanks — please post the draft schema in this thread when ready.

alex (eng-platform): Will do. Short follow-up: we should include a migration plan for existing routes to the new rollout model so customers see no break.

maya (eng-runtime): I'll drop an initial PR with schema + simple simulator tomorrow.

sasha (eng-sre): I'll add the alerts to the alerting repo once the schema exists.

zoe (devex): I'll prototype the modal and the dry-run API contract.

nora (eng-platform): Marking this pinned for visibility.

alex (eng-platform): Great, thanks everyone.
